title: Copilot Studio: block maker-provided credentials for tool authentication
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, credential restriction, default, roles and control paths are supported. Licensing and automation gaps are appropriately narrow; one minor clarification should acknowledge Microsoft's alternative connector authentication label.

claims.claim: Administrators can block makers from choosing maker-provided credentials for agent tools.
claims.quote: Admins can enable and disable the selection of maker-provided credentials in the Power Platform admin center, as described in this article.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A tool configured with maker credentials can give agent users access to data or actions permitted to the maker rather than themselves.
claims.quote: Using maker credentials could lead to oversharing of data or capabilities - for example, an end user might retrieve information or perform actions that only the maker's account is permitted to do.

claims.claim: Control maker credential options lets administrators allow end-user credentials, maker-provided credentials, or both.
claims.quote: You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled by default, so restriction requires administrator configuration.
claims.quote: By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.

claims.claim: When end-user credentials are enforced, no stored maker credentials are used at run time.
claims.quote: No stored maker credentials are used at run time, aligning the agent's behavior with the end user's actual permissions.

claims.claim: End-user authentication limits tool actions to the permissions of the end user's account.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Learn warns that enforcement immediately removes the maker's ability to select their credentials.
claims.quote: When configured as instructed, the feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials for authenticating tools within the environment or environment group.

claims.claim: Enforcing the restriction changes all tools for all agents in the affected environments to require end-user credentials at runtime.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users in new conversations with affected agents are prompted to sign in to connected services if needed.
claims.quote: Enforcing the use of end-user credentials prompts the end user to sign in (to the relevant service or connector) when needed.

claims.claim: The credential policy applies per environment or across all environments in an environment group.
claims.quote: Choose whether end-user or maker credentials (or both) can be selected by makers for agents in an environment, or for all agents in all environments in an environment group.

claims.claim: Environment Admin is the documented permission for configuring a single environment.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator or Global Admin is the documented permission for configuring environment groups.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: An environment in a group must be configured through that group by a tenant admin with access to it.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Environment-group settings override individual environment settings and leave individual configuration options unavailable.
claims.quote: If the environment is in a group, the options are unavailable and a message directs you to configure the setting for the group, not the individual environment.

claims.claim: The activated policy covers both existing and new agents in scope.
claims.quote: Once active, all existing and new agents in that environment adhere to this rule, and the types of authentication options for makers change in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Learn says every tool call requires authentication with a live user sign-in when maker-provided credentials are prevented.
claims.quote: When maker-provided credentials are prevented from being used, agents require real-time user interaction because each tool call must be authenticated with a live user sign-in.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Learn warns that scheduled, autonomous-event and background agents fail due to missing credentials after enforcement.
claims.quote: As a result, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.claim: The credential-control documentation says all agent triggers must involve an active user.
claims.quote: All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Makers whose tools previously used their credentials might be prompted to change the configuration before publishing.
claims.quote: If the maker previously had a tool configured with their credentials, they might be prompted to change it before publishing the agent.

claims.claim: A Power Automate flow used as an agent tool requires each user to sign in for the connections the flow uses.
claims.quote: A Power Automate flow as a tool in the agent also requires each user to sign in for any connections that flow uses.

claims.claim: The authentication-type control covers connectors, built-in actions and embedded Power Automate flows equally.
claims.quote: The control over the authentication type covers connectors, built-in actions, and embedded Power Automate flows equally.

claims.claim: MCP tools are not named on the credential-control Learn page.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio block maker provided credentials pricing license meter exceptions autonomous MCP. Read configure-no-maker-authentication in full: no MCP mention. Other Power Apps MCP pages link to this control.

claims.claim: The credential-control documentation identifies no alternative credential type that remains available after maker-provided credentials are blocked.
claims.quote: Searched: maker-provided credentials exception block. Read configure-no-maker-authentication and add-tools-custom-agent; neither documents another surviving type. Sharing-control system identities concern a different control.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate price for this credential control at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" "pricing". Read configure-no-maker-authentication and billing-licensing: no separate control price; product usage billing is documented separately.

claims.claim: No meter specific to this control is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio block maker provided credentials pricing license meter exceptions autonomous MCP. Read configure-no-maker-authentication and billing-licensing: neither names a meter for configuring this control.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The setting's Learn page lists Power Platform admin permissions as its only prerequisite and names no licence.
claims.quote: Prerequisites: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: The licensing model for this control is not yet published, represented as unknown rather than included or free.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" "pricing". Read configure-no-maker-authentication, billing-licensing and managed-environment-licensing: no control-specific licensing model; managed-environment licensing is explicit.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Environment groups can contain only managed environments.
claims.quote: Environment groups can only contain managed environments.

claims.claim: When managed environments are activated, all active usage requires a qualifying standalone licence or pay-as-you-go meter.
claims.quote: When you activate managed environments in an environment, all active usage requires one of these standalone licenses or pay-as-you-go meters.

claims.claim: Power Apps per app, Power Pages and Copilot Studio pay-as-you-go meters qualify for managed-environment licensing.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go meters for Power Apps per app, Power Pages, and Copilot Studio also qualify.

claims.claim: Configuring an individual environment does not require placing it in a group and does not remove its existing licensing obligations.
claims.quote: Choose whether end-user or maker credentials (or both) can be selected by makers for agents in an environment, or for all agents in all environments in an environment group.

claims.claim: The update might take a minute to propagate.
claims.quote: The update might take a minute to propagate.

claims.claim: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials is an environment-level sharing control for Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: The Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting is an environment-level control for Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The separate sharing control governs publishing and sharing, not an agent's runtime execution.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn't block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.claim: The sharing control does not retroactively unshare existing agents.
claims.quote: The control doesn't retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.

claims.claim: The environment sharing control provides All sharing allowed and Safe sharing enforced modes.
claims.quote: To provide detection and guidance without blocking, select All sharing allowed. Or, to block unsafe sharing paths, select Safe sharing enforced.

claims.claim: All sharing allowed mode supplies guidance that can identify agents and flows relying on embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote: Start in a development or validation environment and select All sharing allowed. Use the resulting guidance to understand which agents and flows rely on embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: The Threat detection sharing-control documentation is preview and subject to change.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The Threat detection sharing control can be configured per environment or per environment group.
claims.quote: You can configure the setting for an individual environment or an environment group.

claims.claim: The maker-side tool authentication field defaults to user authentication.
claims.quote: Authentication: Select whether to use the user's (End user) or maker's (Maker-provided) credentials for the tool. By default, user authentication applies.

claims.claim: The credential restriction is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... Select Environments or Environment groups. ... select Settings ... Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Copilot Studio agents ... Under Control maker credential options

claims.claim: No PowerShell, REST, Power Platform API or pac CLI equivalent for the credential-option control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" "REST" "PowerShell". Read configure-no-maker-authentication and pac copilot-studio search excerpts: consent bypass is a different setting; no credential-policy equivalent found.

claims.claim: The environment sharing setting is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the environment sharing control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" PowerShell API environment settings. Read configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and Power Apps PowerShell search excerpts; no equivalent found.

claims.claim: The group or environment sharing path is Power Platform admin center > Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Environment groups (or Environments) > target > Set up.
claims.quote: select Security, and then select Threat detection. ... Select Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials. ... In the Environment groups tab, select the environment group ... In the Environments tab, select the environment ... Select Set up.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the Threat detection sharing control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials" "API" "PowerShell". Read control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials and sharing-control excerpts; no equivalent API or PowerShell operation found.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio tool Authentication Maker-provided credentials configure API PowerShell. Read add-tools-custom-agent and connector/authentication search excerpts; no equivalent operation found.
